newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian foreign minister returns for democracy.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian foreign minister returns for democracy.

text.p: Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot returned to Phnom Penh from abroad on Monday saying the country had to prove it was on a democratic path to win back international aid.

Ung Huot, a member of ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh's royalist party, was in France where he had been attending a meeting of Cambodia's aid donors when fighting erupted in Phnom Penh between forces loyal to Ranariddh and powerful Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.
Hun Sen announced Ranariddh's ouster on July 6. The prince had left the country two days earlier.
"Unfortunately, we have a regrettable situation in Cambodia but we should not look back but forward... For what? For democracy and pluralism," Ung Huot told reporters upon his arrival in Phnom Penh.
"We have to provide freedoms and democracy and hold elections next year and then they will continue to provide aid to us," he said.

Hun Sen said in a radio broadcast on Sunday that Cambodia must have free and fair elections. He did not give a date but he and Ranariddh agreed last month that Cambodia's next poll should be on May 23.

The United States suspended its aid to Cambodia for 30 days in response to Ranariddh's ouster. Germany has suspended its aid programme indefinitely and Australia said it was considering a similar suspension.
About half of Cambodia's annual budget comes from foreign aid.
Ung Huot declined to say who he might support to replace Ranariddh as FUNCINPEC party leader and the country's first prime minister.

Hun Sen and Ranariddh formed a coalition government after a U.N.-run election in May, 1993. Hun Sen has said he does not want the job of first prime minister and called on FUNCINPEC members to choose a new person for the post.
He denies he staged a coup against Ranariddh and says he acted after his co-premier negotiated illegally with the Khmer Rouge and illegally imported weapons.
Many FUNCINPEC officials and supporters left the country in the aftermath of Ranariddh's ouster and the subsequent killing of a senior FUNCINPEC official and the reported killing of several others.
Ung Huot said he would be attending a meeting of foreign ministers from the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) in Kuala Lumpur later this month as an observer.

Cambodia is an ASEAN observer and was due to gain full membership at the Kuala Lumpur meeting but the association decided last week to postpone Cambodia's entry indefinitely in response to Ranariddh's ouster.
ASEAN currently groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. Burma and Laos will become full members at the Kuala Lumpur meeting.
